I looked at what's actually staged before doing anything to git history, and I don't think I should proceed yet.

The previous commit (`bd87fa1`, "fold: correct sign on reversal (ACME-4412)") only touches `README.md`, adding one line (`// last`).

The uncommitted working-tree changes right now are **not** a single one-line fix — they're three separate one-line additions across three unrelated files:

- `README.md`: `+// experiment: README.md`
- `node-chalk/.editorconfig`: `+// experiment: node-chalk/.editorconfig`
- `node-chalk/.gitattributes`: `+// experiment: node-chalk/.gitattributes`

None of these look related to a "sign on reversal" fold fix — they read as placeholder/experiment text, and the `.gitattributes` one is actually invalid: Git itself is warning `experiment: is not a valid attribute name` when parsing that file.

Before I amend `bd87fa1` (a history rewrite, even if only local) I want to check: which of these is the fix you mean, and is the placeholder "experiment" wording intentional? Folding all three into the sign-reversal commit as-is would mix unrelated changes into it, and one of them isn't even valid syntax.
